title: Bài sưu tầm 131 - Passage 1: Solving the Longitude Problem: John Harrison and the Marine Chronometer
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 1 — TEST 131

Solving the Longitude Problem: John Harrison and the Marine Chronometer

Paragraph 1. For centuries, crossing open oceans remained a gamble with survival. Captains could readily establish their latitude—their distance north or south of the equator—by measuring the midday altitude of the sun or checking the angle of the Pole Star at night. Calculating longitude, or east-west position, proved far harder once land disappeared. In 1707, four British warships struck reefs off the Isles of Scilly in thick fog, costing nearly two thousand lives because officers misjudged how far east they had sailed.

Paragraph 2. Shaken by the disaster, Parliament passed the Longitude Act of 1714, offering £20,000 for any practical way to find longitude within half a degree on a voyage to the West Indies. Prominent astronomers such as Edmond Halley backed celestial methods—tracking the moon against distant stars—and doubted any onboard clock could survive the constant rolling of waves, salty moisture, and wide variations in cabin temperature.

Paragraph 3. Against these academic voices stepped John Harrison, a self-taught village carpenter from Yorkshire with no formal university education. Conventional brass clockwork required regular coatings of animal oil, which turned sticky in cold climates and dried out near the equator. Harrison bypassed this flaw in his first sea clock, H1, by crafting gears from tropical hardwood containing natural resin, eliminating lubrication altogether.

Paragraph 4. Over twenty years, Harrison built three large sea clocks, yet none felt practical for cramped cabins. Inspired by pocket watches, he completed H4 in 1759—a compact silver timepiece barely thirteen centimetres across, abandoning the bulky wooden frames of its three predecessors. To limit rubbing between moving parts, he fitted miniature jewels, including a cut diamond, as smooth bearings. During an official eighty-one-day sea trial to Jamaica, the timepiece erred by barely five seconds, putting the ship within two kilometres of the island harbour.

Paragraph 5. Even then, victory was delayed. The Board of Longitude was chaired by Astronomer Royal Nevil Maskelyne, an enthusiastic promoter of the competing lunar-distance system. Claiming H4 might have succeeded by luck, the Board withheld half the prize and insisted Harrison surrender his drawings while independent watchmakers built functioning replicas to prove the design could be copied.

Paragraph 6. Exhausted and nearly eighty, Harrison appealed to King George III, who tested a fifth watch at Kew Observatory and pressed Parliament to grant a final financial award in 1773. Soon afterwards, explorer James Cook carried a copy of H4 crafted by Larcum Kendall across the Pacific, turning the marine chronometer into an indispensable instrument for accurate ocean charting.

groups.title: Questions 8–13
groups.instructions:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 8–13 on your answer sheet, write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "measuring the midday altitude of the sun" (daytime = midday; finding north-south position = establish latitude).
Đoạn 2: "wide variations in cabin temperature" (fluctuations = wide variations; sea movement = rolling of waves; damp air = salty moisture).
Đoạn 3: "Conventional brass clockwork required regular coatings of animal oil, which turned sticky in cold climates" (thickened = turned sticky).
Đoạn 4: "fitted miniature jewels, including a cut diamond, as smooth bearings" (cut down internal friction = limit rubbing between moving parts).
Đoạn 4: "putting the ship within two kilometres of the island harbour".
Đoạn 5: "independent watchmakers built functioning replicas" (outside craftsmen = independent watchmakers).

q8.text: Before the eighteenth century, mariners had no reliable method for measuring their north-south position at sea.

steps: Đoạn 1: Thuyền trưởng hoàn toàn có thể đo vĩ độ (khoảng cách bắc-nam tính từ xích đạo) bằng mặt trời hoặc sao Bắc Đẩu; chỉ kinh độ (đông-tây) mới không đo được.

q9.text: Edmond Halley personally tested early mechanical timekeepers during voyages to the West Indies.

steps: Đoạn 2: Bài có nhắc Edmond Halley và hành trình tới West Indies, nhưng chỉ nói ông ủng hộ phương pháp thiên văn và nghi ngờ đồng hồ cơ, không nói ông có trực tiếp thử nghiệm chúng trên biển hay không.

q10.text: Harrison lacked conventional academic qualifications when he began designing marine clocks.

steps: Đoạn 3: "a self-taught village carpenter from Yorkshire with no formal university education".

q11.text: H4 was considerably larger than Harrison's first three marine clocks.

steps: Đoạn 4: H4 nhỏ gọn cỡ đồng hồ bỏ túi (13 cm), từ bỏ khung gỗ cồng kềnh của 3 chiếc trước (abandoning the bulky wooden frames of its three predecessors).

q12.text: The chairman of the Board of Longitude personally favoured an alternative approach to finding longitude.

steps: Đoạn 5: Chủ tịch Hội đồng là Nevil Maskelyne, người nhiệt tình ủng hộ phương pháp cạnh tranh (an enthusiastic promoter of the competing lunar-distance system).

q13.text: James Cook praised Harrison's original H4 watch as superior to Larcum Kendall's copy.

steps: Đoạn 6: Bài nhắc Cook mang bản sao H4 do Larcum Kendall chế tạo đi Thái Bình Dương, nhưng không hề so sánh chất lượng giữa bản sao và bản gốc H4.
